method: A fresh-context Codex native agent received only the Skill path and a Level 2 delivery-planning request. It performed no file changes, production actions, or external calls.
request: Replace a payment settlement schema with a 40M-row backfill, rotate a production webhook secret, upgrade an advised transitive SDK dependency, and roll out a feature-flagged worker in a shared repository with existing CI, migrations, dashboards, and secrets management.
observed_decisions: Classified the request as Level 2 and separated unknown repository facts from proposed controls.
Used six atomic PRs for compatible expansion, SDK upgrade, secret rotation support, backfill, worker rollout, and later cleanup rather than one mixed change.
Applied expand-migrate-contract with version-aware readers, deliberate dual-write or derived-write policy, resumable idempotent backfill, stop thresholds, and deferred old-schema removal.
Kept the worker flag disabled on deployment, used staged tenant/shard/percentage rollout, monitored outcome/queue/provider signals, and disabled the flag before deployment rollback.
Required fake secrets and fixtures for local reproduction, while prohibiting production credentials or secret values in source, logs, evidence, and test output.
Required manifest/lockfile review, advisory evidence, compatibility tests, rollback, operator runbooks, PR evidence, and CI without assuming exact commands or tools.
required_evidence: Git diff, commit IDs, PR scope, CI result, and independent review.
Migration dry-run, compatibility and idempotency tests, backup/restore validation for destructive work, and cleanup condition.
Redacted secret/config validation, dependency/security signal, rollout metrics, stop condition, and rollback/recovery evidence.
Local setup/check/test output using non-secret configuration and minimal fixture data.
limitations: The agent produced a design and acceptance-test plan because the visible workspace did not contain the described payments service.
This qualitative forward test does not prove the presence, correctness, or performance of a real migration runner, feature flag, secrets manager, SDK scan, CI system, or production rollout.
